purpose: Durable, versioned register of lazysite security-review rounds. One record per round: scope, coverage (so a future run can deliberately repeat, skip, or extend an area), findings with severity and the release that fixed them, and root-cause themes to re-verify. Detailed per-round exploit reports are delivered as files and NOT committed here.

practice.cadence: Reviewed regularly (target: weekly). Releases are cut from findings + fixes; a security release records every fixed issue in CHANGELOG.md in detail.
practice.method: A fan-out of review agents (static across every surface + black-box probers on a live multi-account, multi-site instance), plus focused follow-ups when a class warrants it (e.g. an RCE/OS-access deep dive). Serious findings are verified by reproduction before they are trusted.
practice.coverage_rule: Each round marks the areas it covered. A subsequent round should either extend an already-covered area (deeper/different angle) or move to an areas_not_covered candidate, so the corpus of checks grows rather than repeats blindly.
practice.reports_location: Out-of-repo files (carry live exploit detail); this register carries only severity + title + status.

rounds.scope: 8-agent review (6 static: core processor+multisite, auth/session/oauth, manager-api+access-control, dav/mcp/tokens, all plugins, xss/injection/upload; 2 black-box probers) + 3-agent RCE/OS-access follow-up (exec primitives, write->exec chains [verified], deployment misconfig).
root_cause_themes: A: cookie-path authorization not at parity with the token %need map (yields takeover + escalation + the plugin-runner RCE gate)
B: bare-prefix path confinement (index($real,$root) without trailing slash) recurring across the manager file layer and the include/json resolvers
C: escape-at-sink discipline + no CSP; active-content writes (.shtml/.htaccess/.cgi) not blocked
D: dev-server and shipped vhost templates not at parity with production hardening (SSI #exec, AllowOverride All, 0.0.0.0 bind)

findings.title: Plugin runner executes an attacker-named file as Perl (resolve_plugin_script no confinement); any ui account writes Perl into a non-.pl file then plugin-action runs it
Account takeover: any interactive account resets any password (cmd_passwd called without actor; no cookie manage_users gate)
:::include / json: reads lazysite/auth/.secret -> session forgery (confines to $DOCROOT, not the lazysite tree, nor $croot)
SSI #exec RCE: vhost templates ship Options +Includes on the writable docroot and .shtml is not blocked -> manage_content partner writes evil.shtml (Apache)
.htaccess handler injection: AllowOverride All + a saved .htaccess (AddHandler cgi-script .txt) -> CGI (Apache)
Cookie sessions bypass the capability model: %need is token-only; editor did config-set/backup/domains-list/user-enum
CSRF gate is POST-only; mutating actions work over GET (config-set proven via GET)
validate_path sibling-prefix docroot escape (index($real,$DOCROOT) no trailing slash) -> write outside docroot via MCP/API
File-editor deny-list gaps: reads lazysite.conf/templates/full-backups/audit.log/plugin-secret confs
Stored+reflected XSS in manager breadcrumb (files.md:170 unescaped path/label)
Front-matter title/subtitle emitted unescaped in every layout -> content-author XSS
Uploads: active-content extensions (html/svg/js/shtml) not blocked, served same-origin
findings.note: Active server-executed uploads (.shtml/.cgi/.php/.htaccess) blocked. .html/.svg/.js are legitimate publishable content, so they are NOT blocked; a response CSP is the proportionate follow-up mitigation for author-published active content.

findings.title: SSRF guard validates only the initial URL; LWP follows redirects to internal targets
Dev server serve_static: unauthenticated arbitrary file read (../etc/passwd, /lazysite/auth/users); binds 0.0.0.0
Cross-domain :::include/json (confine $DOCROOT not $croot)
dav_scope not enforced on MCP/API (only WebDAV)
Logout does not invalidate the session (sid stays in registry; cookie valid 24h)
Group membership carried in cookie and trusted 24h (demotion delayed)
Backup restore tar xzf --no-same-owner keeps setuid/setgid, no symlink guard (root --restore-full)
Save path calls is_blocked_config without ext check -> .cgi/.PL/.shtml/.htaccess pass save
lazysite@.service has no NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem/PrivateTmp/RestrictSUIDSGID
CSRF token user+hour scoped, not session-scoped (survives logout <=2h)
findings.note: M4 (revoke on logout) now kills the session server-side, so a surviving CSRF token rides a dead cookie and is unusable; full per-session scoping deferred to a later round.

findings.title: Login rate limit per-IP only, fails open; no per-account counter
findings.note: Fail-open is a deliberate availability choice (a broken limiter must not lock out all logins); a per-account counter + fail-closed-with-bound is future work.

findings.title: OAuth PKCE not re-asserted on consent POST; unauthenticated register has no rate limit (store growth)
findings.note: Consent-POST PKCE gap is unredeemable (not exploitable); register rate-limit is store-growth hardening. Both deferred.

findings.title: plugins.md uses a weak esc() in attribute contexts
Secret files open()'d then chmod'd (TOCTOU window; shielded by 02770 dir)
findings.note: Practical risk neutralised by the 02770 auth dir (world cannot traverse it); an atomic O_EXCL-create rewrite is deferred to avoid destabilising concurrent secret creation in a security release.

findings.title: Alias-redirect body echoes $canon unescaped (manager-controlled source)
Plain-CGI shares one www-data across sites; secrets group-readable -> document 'plain CGI is not a tenant boundary'
Dev server login POST without ?action=login self-execs in a loop and wedges

resolution.note: All critical/high/medium findings fixed and covered by regression tests. Low/info: XSS-escape + dev-server + systemd items fixed; login-throttle and OAuth-register hardening deferred (availability trade-off / not exploitable); secret-file chmod TOCTOU accepted (shielded by the 02770 dir); CSRF session-scope mitigated by M4 revoke-on-logout. H5c uploads: active server-content blocked, .html/.svg/.js remain publishable content with a CSP follow-up.
